articles.title: Democrats Now Have the Power to Nullify the Electoral College. Here’s How
articles.summary: After flipping several key state legislatures and gubernatorial seats in this month’s elections , Democrats now have a path to nullify an institution of U.S. elections that has cost the party at least two presidential contests so far this century: the Electoral College. articles.title: The U.S. Has Lost Its Measles-Elimination Status. Here’s What That Means
articles.summary: For more than a quarter of a century, the U.S. has held measles-elimination status, meaning the virus was no longer spreading continuously within the country. Prior to the introduction of the first measles vaccine in 1963, nearly all American children contracted the disease before they were 15, for an annual case count of up to four million, including 400 to 500 deaths and 48,000 hospitalizations. articles.title: What Is the Kerch Bridge—and Why Does Ukraine Keep Attacking It?

articles.title: Measles Has Returned
articles.summary: In 2000, the United States achieved a remarkable public health milestone: eliminating the continuous spread of measles within our borders. For 26 years—through Republican and Democratic administrations, pandemics, wars, and recessions—that achievement stood. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has officially stripped the United States of its measles elimination status after a resurgence of cases infecting more than 7,000 Americans over the past two years. Measles is once again considered endemic in America.
